answer: A sybil farmer mints identities cheaply inside one economy, but cannot cheaply mint a three-year contribution history on an independent network with its own admission costs. Let admission require an imported, signature-bound credential from outside, a lotus rooted in another pond's mud. One external history anchors exactly one local identity, so a copied credential is an echo of the original and is rejected, and each genuine pearl of outside standing buys a single seat. The attack then pays every other network's price at once, which no farm can afford at scale.
